newsitem.title: UK: BT to run UK's military phone system.
newsitem.headline: BT to run UK's military phone system.

text.p: The British government said on Wednesday that it had chosen a consortium led by British Telecommunications Plc to take over and run its armed forces telephone network in Britain.
The change is designed to modernise services and to cut the armed forces' telephone bill by 15 percent to about 85 million pounds a year, government officials said.
Defence Secretary Michael Portillo said in a written parliamentary answer that the initial contract would be worth 700 million pounds ($1.15 billion).
Ministry of Defence (MOD) officials and BT later said the overall value of the contract would be closer to one billion pounds once user tariffs were taken into account.
The award is still subject to final negotiations but the officials told reporters the government expects a contract will be signed in time for BT to start work next April.
Other members of the consortium include U.S. company Lockheed Martin and British firm GEC-Marconi, a unit of the General Electric Co Plc .
The BT bid was chosen in preference to a rival offer from a consortium led by Racal Electronics Plc and including British firms W.S. Atkins and Logica.
"The BT solution had the edge in being cheaper and in offering more facilities," a senior ministry official told reporters.
The award is part of the government's Private Finance Initiative aimed at privatising the financing and associated risk of capital projects in the public sector.
Under the deal BT and its partners will provide the armed forces with voice and data services by taking over and transforming the five existing armed forces networks in Britain into a single system.
Government officials said it will be up to BT to decide how it does this but some 1,200 civilian and military staff currently employed in running the network would be affected.
They said some of the civilian staff were expected to be transferred to the private sector but details still had to be worked out in negotiations BT.
BT said in a statement: "Many new job opportunities will be created by the project and a considerable number of MOD people involved with the existing network will be transferred."
"We are delighted that the MOD has selected BT as prime contractor," said Tom Johnson, head of BT's government business.

"Our offer combines BT's technological expertise with an innovative commercial approach to give a solution which will provide the UK's armed forces with substantial operational and financial benefits into the next century."
